additions.name: SNC PARAY DC — planned 55 MW IT data centre (12 data halls, Hines) on the former Air France training site

status.summary: The MRAe Île-de-France delegated opinion no. 019554/GUNENV of 14 August 2026 names the data-centre project of SNC PARAY DC (with RTE for the grid connection) at Paray-Vieille-Poste (Essonne), within a building-permit procedure: a main building with IT halls (15,260 m2 footprint, 25,735 m2 of floor), 43 emergency generators of 292 MW thermal, 48 chillers and an RTE substation on the northern parcel of the former Air France training site, whose buildings are to be demolished. The project is therefore announced as of 14 August 2026. No building permit, environmental authorisation or physical work is established; the late-2028/early-2029 grid connection is a forecast.

locator.precision: Centroid of cadastral parcel AB 53 in Paray-Vieille-Poste (3.4 ha, about 233 by 207 m), the single parcel named by the applicant, of which the project uses 29,655 m2 at 1 avenue du Maréchal Devaux. It locates the data-centre plot, not the building.
locator.identity_review: The MRAe opinion of 14 August 2026 names the SNC PARAY DC data centre on the northern parcel of the former Air France training site at Paray-Vieille-Poste. The applicant's note in the same portal dossier (24840) gives the address 1 avenue du Maréchal Devaux and states that the project covers 29,655 m2 on part of a single cadastral parcel, AB 53, owned by Air France under a promise of sale to SNC PARAY DC, bounded by rue des Avernaises, avenue du Maréchal Devaux, rue Jean Mermoz and rue Marcel Albert. API Carto returns parcel 91479000AB0053 with a contenance of 33,721 m2; its centroid lies inside it, 71 m from its boundary. The BAN point of 1 avenue du Maréchal Devaux lies 27.5 m east of the parcel on the avenue, and the Géorisques point of the Air France real-estate record at the same address lies 78 m south of it. The commune centre is not used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is the centroid of a 3.4 ha parcel whose vertices lie up to 146 m away, and the building position on it is not published in a georeferenced form.

additions.site_name: Edged Data Center Marseille, former Saint-Louis Sucre refinery (336 rue de Lyon, Marseille 15e)
additions.name: Edged Marseille Saint-Louis — planned nine-hall data centre (R+3) with 12 emergency generators (ESL PROPERTIES, Edged Energy)

status.summary: The MRAe Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur opinion nos. 020291/GUNENV and 020695/A P, adopted on 1 September 2026, concerns the creation of a data centre by ESL PROPERTIES, a subsidiary of Edged Energy, on the former Saint-Louis Sucre factory site in Marseille 15e: an R+3 building with nine IT halls, twelve emergency generators of 8.16 MW thermal each, rooftop chillers, an HTB/HTA substation and a waste-heat building on a 17,156 m2 plot, under a building-permit and environmental-authorisation application filed on 25 November 2025 and completed on 18 June 2026. The project is therefore announced as of 1 September 2026. No environmental authorisation, permit in effect or physical work is established; the planned fourth-quarter 2026 start and 24-month works are forecasts.

locator.precision: Centroid of the union of cadastral parcels 899 E 81 and 899 E 82 of Marseille 15e (4.4 ha, about 219 by 403 m), the northern lot of the former Saint-Louis Sucre refinery between rue de Lyon and the Aygalades stream that holds the data centre and the Studios de la Méditerranée. The 17,156 m2 data-centre plot is the north-eastern part of the lot along the stream; on figure 3 of the MRAe opinion it approximately coincides with parcel E 82, which lies 38 to 204 m from the point (its centroid 77 m), so the data-centre building may lie about 40 to 200 m from the point.
locator.identity_review: The MRAe opinion of 1 September 2026 and the applicant's summary place the ESL PROPERTIES (Edged Energy) data centre at 336 rue de Lyon on the former Saint-Louis Sucre site, within a 46,807 m2 landholding shared with the Studios de la Méditerranée; no parcel list is published. The applicant's 'Projet global' plan shows the northern lot bounded by rue de Lyon, by labelled parcels 899 E 6, 7, 10-16, 20, 21 and 23, by the Aygalades stream with parcels 899 E 37, 50, 63-65 and 69 beyond it, by parcels 57 and 59 and by the July 2025 limit of the northern lot. In the current cadastre the parcels lying between rue de Lyon, the stream strip, those northern neighbours and the southern lot are E 81 (31,193 m2) and E 82 (13,104 m2), totalling 44,297 m2 (95% of the declared landholding; the small parcels E 79 and E 88-90 to their east are not included); the southern lot E 74 holds the BAN point of 336 rue de Lyon and the Géorisques point of SAINT LOUIS SUCRE, both 13 m south of the union. The SDES register's April 2026 permit to FONCIERE SAINT LOUIS at 336 rue de Lyon (48,857 m2, parcels H 115, E 58, E 56) matches the studio developer's landholding under its earlier parcel numbers. Figure 3 of the MRAe opinion (taken from the applicant's presentation note) colours the data-centre operation as a strip along the stream at the northern end of the site and the studios between it and rue de Lyon, with the logistics centre and the part of the refinery that stays active to the south; registered on the cadastre by rotation and two corner points (north tip, southern corner on rue de Lyon), those areas fall on E 82, on E 81, and on E 74 with its small neighbours E 79 and E 88-90 respectively. The parcel selection is therefore an inference from the applicant's plans, not a declared list; the commune centre, the company address and the whole-refinery address point are not used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is the centroid of a 4.4 ha two-parcel lot whose vertices lie up to 204 m away, the parcels are identified by matching the applicant's plan rather than from a declared list, and the data-centre building position is not published in a georeferenced form.

status.summary: Global Switch's Madrid page, in the version modified on 23 September 2026, describes the facility in the present tense (Global Switch Madrid offers location, low power pricing, enterprise ecosystems and client solutions, supports a wide range of power requirements and 'offers an exceptional choice and range of connectivity partners'); the site navigation lists Madrid among the operator's data centres while Johor and Bangkok are marked 'Coming Soon'.
